content:
Kevin Osei: circling back on SUP-18510 + a few customer asks this week — we need to settle on `event_id` generation. UUIDv4 vs ULID came up again. Also: what do we tell customers to dedupe in SIEM when exporter retries.

Marcus Lin: +1. requirement from my side: stable id across retries, and something customers can use as a primary key. also needs to be easy for us to generate in all services + private installer.

Hanae Suzuki: what are the constraints from Splunk/Sentinel? do they care about format? mostly string, right.

Kevin Osei: mostly string. the practical issue is ordering + readability. ULID gives time-sort and still unique. UUIDv4 is fine but not sortable so incident investigations are a little worse (esp when you’re looking at raw logs).

Allison Grant: also: ingestion pipelines sometimes bucket/partition by time; ULID helps for backfills / replay debugging since lexicographic sort ~ timestamp. not a hard req but nice.

Logan Wright: from telemetry/dashboards POV: we mostly group on `event_type` and tenant. `event_id` mainly for dedupe and drill-down. orderability is a nice-to-have.

Nadia Rahman: schema-wise we can declare `event_id` as required string, and allow both formats. but we should pick “preferred” for new producers.

Sean Gallagher: reminder: delivery is at-least-once for a bunch of paths (buffer + retry) so duplicates are expected sometimes. key is: the duplicate should carry the same `event_id`.

Kevin Osei: exactly. exporter currently wraps failures and re-sends. if producer generates a new ID on each send attempt, dedupe is impossible. we need to lock the semantics:
- producer generates `event_id` once per logical audit event
- any retries / replays must re-use the same `event_id`

Marcus Lin: can we enforce that via library? e.g., the audit emitter takes an `event_id` optional param, else it generates. but on retry it should pass through.

Kevin Osei: in hosted services yes. for private installer it’s trickier (bash/go tooling). but same rule: when we spool to disk / queue, store event_id with the record.

Hanae Suzuki: what about “idempotency key” vs event_id? do we need both?

Kevin Osei: my take: `event_id` is the canonical unique identifier of an emitted event. an `idempotency_key` is an optional producer-side thing for “don’t emit twice for same request” (like admin button double-click). but customers should dedupe on `event_id`, not idempotency_key.

Allison Grant: +1. and `idempotency_key` can be missing. `event_id` must never be missing.

Nadia Rahman: so proposal:
- choose ULID for new events as default generator in shared lib
- allow UUID input (some legacy producers already have it)
- JSON schema can validate either pattern, but documentation says “ULID recommended; UUID accepted”.

Logan Wright: +1 ULID. also helps with “grep around a time range” when you only have IDs.

Sean Gallagher: any risks w ULID collisions? (shouldn’t be with decent entropy) but don’t want a compliance footgun.

Kevin Osei: ULID spec includes randomness; collision risk negligible. we can use monotonic ULID generator in-process to avoid same-ms issues. and still treat it as opaque string.

Marcus Lin: ok. what about customer guidance for SIEM duplicates? need something crisp for Naomi/Support.

Dev Patel: yes please. Support keeps getting “why do I see duplicates” and right now we’re hand-waving.

Kevin Osei: suggested wording:
- Redwood audit delivery is at-least-once; during transient failures retries may create duplicate deliveries of the *same* event.
- Each logical event has a stable `event_id`. Customers should configure dedupe on `event_id`.
- For SIEM queries:
  - Splunk: `... | dedup event_id | sort 0 -_time`
  - Sentinel (KQL): `... | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by event_id`
- If customer wants strict exactly-once, they need dedupe on ingest.

Hanae Suzuki: can we also mention scoping? like “unique per tenant”. sometimes customers ask if `event_id` is globally unique.

Nadia Rahman: we can say globally unique, but recommend dedupe by `(tenant_id, event_id)` just to be safe in multi-tenant pipelines.

Allison Grant: +1 include tenant_id anyway; it’s in schema. also: make sure we don’t call it “GUID” in docs. keep it consistent: `event_id`.

Sean Gallagher: and we should be explicit: duplicates should have identical `event_id` but *may* have different `exported_at` or ingestion timestamps. don’t compare the SIEM event time.

Kevin Osei: good call. also exporter could add `delivery_attempt`? but that’s extra cardinality/noise. i’d avoid putting attempt count into the payload customers see.

Marcus Lin: agree — avoid attempt counters. we can keep exporter metrics internal.

Logan Wright: one more: do we need `event_hash` as fallback if someone loses event_id? (e.g., legacy)

Kevin Osei: rather fix legacy to supply `event_id`. hash-based dedupe is messy and risky (collisions, also changes if any field changes).

Hanae Suzuki: ok.

Marcus Lin: decision: default `event_id` = ULID (preferred), accept UUID for legacy; requirement: stable across retries. Kevin can you add a short section to the exporter guidance doc + PR comment?

Kevin Osei: yep. I’ll update exporter docs + ping Elliot for the customer-facing snippet. also adding a check in exporter: if incoming event has no event_id, reject + metric (so we catch producers that forgot).

Allison Grant: please make sure rejection doesn’t drop critical audit events silently. if we reject, we need to surface loudly.

Sean Gallagher: +1. emit to DLQ + page only if rate crosses threshold.

Kevin Osei: ack. best effort: DLQ + metric + alert (not paging on single event). will coordinate w Aisha/Sean.

Dev Patel: once doc snippet is ready, I’ll add to Support macros for “SIEM duplicates” responses.

Marcus Lin: cool. closing the loop: Kevin create a follow-up in ENG-4821/ENG-4827 notes so it doesn’t get lost.

Kevin Osei: done, will link in Linear + drop draft wording here later today.

Hanae Suzuki: :thumbsup:

Logan Wright: :+1: 

Allison Grant: :white_check_mark:
